findings.statement: Marketing exceeded its budget by the largest amount.
findings.method: SQL join and calculation of overspend
findings.code: SELECT department, budget, actual, (actual - budget) AS overspend FROM budget_2025_budget b JOIN budget_2025_actual a USING (department) ORDER BY overspend DESC LIMIT 1

findings.statement: All departments’ overspend values were computed and Marketing had the highest.
findings.method: SQL join and ordering by overspend
findings.code: SELECT department, budget, actual, (actual - budget) AS overspend FROM budget_2025_budget b JOIN budget_2025_actual a USING (department) ORDER BY overspend DESC

data_quality_notes: budget_2025_budget: 0 nulls, 0 duplicates, budget column type int64, no type problems.
budget_2025_actual: 0 nulls, 0 duplicates, actual column type int64, no type problems.
assumptions: Department names match exactly between the two sheets.
Overspend is calculated as actual spending minus budgeted amount.
limitations: Only 8 departments are present, so the sample size is small.
No outlier detection was performed beyond the basic profile.
